# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz does not bump the facade for a sibling version that is already at target when the PR merges, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs. (`dependencies_update = true` only makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`; it does not cascade version bumps.)
- **A breaking bump of a crate needs a breaking bump of each crate that depends on it.** release-plz gives a dependent without its own commits only a patch bump (release-plz#1599), and users then get two copies of the crate. The `fmt` job runs `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh` to enforce this. See `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md` → "A breaking change in a crate with dependents".
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

Provenance headers for wire-format fixtures follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures".

## Cargo.lock

Committed (workspace contains a binary).

None of these needs a new design.

  ### BLOCKER
  None.
  
  ### MAJOR
  - **The release-plz reason is wrong when compared with repo history** - The spec says that a change to the root `Cargo.toml` only gives no release of sessions-postgres (spec lines 54-57). The repo shows the opposite. Root-only pin changes gave the auto entry "update Cargo.toml dependencies" in two places:
    - `sessions-postgres` 0.1.10 (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/CHANGELOG.md:47-49`, from #351).

    The SMA-763 spec states this as a constraint (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-763-remove-rustsec-2026-0459-ignore-design.md:96-99`). Its non-goal (line 82-83) left `sessions-postgres/Cargo.toml` unchanged, and that crate was still released. The runbook says that release-plz compares each package with its registry copy (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:73`). Note that the precedent is a version-requirement change. I did not confirm that a change to features only gives the same dependency diff.
  
    The current `sessions-postgres/Cargo.toml:18` comment does not name `sqlite`, so it is not wrong today. The edit in design item 4 is therefore only a release trigger, and the spec describes it as a side effect ("anyway").
  
    | Why it matters: The spec writes a wrong model of release-plz into the record. A later ticket can use that model to plan a release that does not occur, or to skip a check. A reviewer can also ask to drop the comment edit because it looks cosmetic.
  
    | Suggested fix: Rewrite the constraint and name both triggers: (a) a commit that touches the crate directory, and (b) release-plz's diff of the inherited dependency list. Keep the per-crate edits as a second, independent trigger, and say that the comment edit exists for this reason. Make the after-merge check in the next finding the real safeguard.
  
  - **Goal 4 has no verification and no after-merge step** - Goal 4 (spec lines 29-30) is the result that users see. The Verification section (lines 109-120) has no step for it. SMA-763 had both checks: `cargo package -p <crate> --no-verify` plus a read of the Cargo.toml inside the archive (SMA-763 spec lines 114-120), and "Confirm that the release-plz PR bumps …" (lines 141-145).
  
    | Why it matters: If the release PR leaves out sessions-postgres, crates.io keeps the manifest with SQLite and no gate goes red.
  
    | Suggested fix: Add three checks:
    - Before merge: run `cargo package -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres --no-verify`. Read `paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres-0.3.1/Cargo.toml` from `target/package/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres-0.3.1.crate`, using exact names and no globs. Confirm that the `[dependencies.sqlx]` features do not include `sqlite`. Do the same for sessions-sqlite and evals, and confirm that `sqlite` is present.
    - After merge: confirm that the release PR bumps sessions-postgres, sessions-sqlite, evals, the facade and the CLI. Watch the CI of that PR.
    - After publish: make a scratchpad project that depends only on `paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres = "=0.3.2"`. Confirm that `cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys -e normal,build` prints nothing. Alternatively, query the crates.io dependencies API with a custom User-Agent.
  
  - **The guard as written passes when cargo fails** - Design item 5 says "test the output, not the exit code" (line 91-92) and "the same shape as the existing axum" step. That step is `if cargo tree … | grep -q …; then exit 1` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/.github/workflows/ci.yml:196`). The job sets no `shell:`, so the step runs with `bash -e` and without `pipefail`. If `cargo tree` exits non-zero, grep gets no input and the step passes.
  
    `cargo tree -i X` stops with an error when X matches no package in the lockfile, for example after a typo, or after a move from libsqlite3-sys to a different SQLite binding. Two versions of libsqlite3-sys cannot occur, because the crate declares `links = "sqlite3"` (SMA-763 spec lines 76-78). The vendored-protox step (ci.yml:209) fails correctly when cargo fails only because it checks that a feature is present. The repo standard is that a guard fails when it cannot read its input (release-ascend.md:63).
  
    | Why it matters: This guard is the only control against the regression. If it passes without a check, the control is gone and nothing shows it.
  
    | Suggested fix: Test the exit code and stdout together. Read stdout only. The text `warning: nothing to print.` goes to stderr (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-temporalio-1.0-lockstep-bump.md:18`). If the builder merges stderr into stdout, a "not empty" test always fails. For example:
    ```bash
    out="$(cargo tree --color never -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres -e normal,build --target all -i libsqlite3-sys)"
    if [ -n "$out" ]; then echo "::error::…"; echo "$out"; exit 1; fi
    ```
    Under `bash -e`, the assignment stops the step if cargo fails. State in the spec which stream the test reads.
  
  - **The new per-crate rule has no CI gate, and a regression shows only during publish** - After this change, `features = ["sqlite"]` in sessions-sqlite and evals is necessary. Every CI build unifies features across the workspace: `test` and `clippy` use `--workspace --all-features` (ci.yml:167). If one of the two crates loses the feature, the other crate supplies it, and CI stays green. The spec checks this only once, by hand (lines 116-117).
  
    Example of the failure: evals loses the feature. The publish verify of evals builds with default features (`default = []`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/crates/paigasus-helikon-evals/Cargo.toml:15`), so it passes and evals is published. The CLI uses `trace-sqlite` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/crates/paigasus-helikon-cli/Cargo.toml:25`), so the CLI publish verify then fails. The result is a partial publish.
  
    | Why it matters: A broken evals goes to crates.io, and the release run stops in the middle.
  
    | Suggested fix: Add a positive check to the same step. It needs no build. These two commands must print a tree:
    - `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys`
    - `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-evals --features trace-sqlite -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys`
  
    On every run, this also proves that the command form still finds libsqlite3-sys. It catches a change in the output format, ANSI color codes (`CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always` is set at ci.yml:24), or a package rename.
  
  - **Patch is the correct call, but the upgrade note has no place** - I agree with patch, not breaking:
    - The API of sessions-postgres does not change.
    - A downstream crate that got `sqlx::sqlite` through feature unification depended on a side effect that we did not document.
    - A breaking bump would force a breaking bump of the facade through `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh`, with no change to the API.
  
    But the only notice to users is the squash title (spec lines 52-53). release-plz writes that one line into all three CHANGELOGs, and "the feature is gone" is false for sessions-sqlite and evals. The spec also names only the compile failure. There is a second failure mode: a downstream crate that uses sqlx `any` with a `sqlite:` URL compiles, then fails at runtime. The reason is that `install_default_drivers` lists the SQLite driver only under `#[cfg(feature = "_sqlite")]` (`/Users/smaschek/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-0.9.1/src/any/mod.rs:44-45`).
  
    | Why it matters: Without the note, users who are affected get no instructions, and two CHANGELOGs get a false line.
  
    | Suggested fix: On the feature branch, add a hand-written entry under `## [Unreleased]` in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/CHANGELOG.md`. Say that sessions-postgres no longer turns on the sqlx `sqlite` feature. Say that a crate which uses `sqlx::sqlite`, or `AnyPool` with a `sqlite:` URL, must add `features = ["sqlite"]` to its own sqlx dependency. Do not edit the release PR instead: release-plz loses that edit when it makes the PR again (release-ascend.md:59). Write the PR title so that it is true in all three CHANGELOGs. CHANGELOG.md is a packaged file, so this entry also gives a second release trigger that does not depend on the comment edit.
  
  ### MINOR
  - **No commit scope is named, and `sessions-postgres` is not an allowed scope** - The allowed scopes are in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/.versionrc:18` and `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/.github/workflows/pr-title.yml:59-64`. | Why it matters: The obvious title `fix(sessions-postgres): …` fails the commit-msg hook and the `pr-title` gate. | Suggested fix: Name the scope in the spec, for example `fix(sessions): SMA-822 move the sqlx sqlite feature out of the workspace base`.
  - **The runbook edit is necessary, not optional** - Design item 7 adds the edit only "if that section lists its steps". It does: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md:11` lists each step of `build-no-default-features`. | Suggested fix: Make item 7 mandatory, and remove it from "Left to the builder".
  - **The guard command does not use `--target all` or `--color never`** - The root `Cargo.toml` prescribes `--target all` for this type of check (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/Cargo.toml:133-136`). The workflow sets `CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always`. | Why it matters: Without `--target all`, a SQLite edge that exists only on a different target is not seen. If cargo adds color to its output, a test for "not present" can pass by mistake. | Suggested fix: Add both flags to both commands.
  - **The root manifest has no comment about the rule** - The `sqlx` entry (`Cargo.toml:81-84`) does not say why `sqlite` is absent from the base. | Why it matters: A later edit can put `sqlite` back "for consistency", and the developer finds the reason only when CI fails. | Suggested fix: Add a comment that follows the Temporal pattern at `Cargo.toml:151-153`. Say that only sessions-sqlite and evals/`trace-sqlite` turn on `sqlite` (SMA-822), and that a `build-no-default-features` step fails if SQLite gets into sessions-postgres.
  - **No check that `Cargo.lock` stays the same** - Features are not recorded in the lockfile, so `Cargo.lock` must not change. | Suggested fix: Add the SMA-763 check, `git diff --exit-code "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" -- Cargo.lock` (SMA-763 spec lines 100-104).
  - **No rollback section** - A revert in the repository does not change manifests that are already on crates.io. | Suggested fix: Add a rollback section. State the steps: add `"sqlite"` back to the crate's own sqlx features, release 0.3.3, and let the facade cascade follow.
  - **One verification item adds nothing** - `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-evals --no-default-features` (line 118) is the same as a plain build, because `default = []`. | Suggested fix: Remove it, or replace it with the positive `trace-sqlite` tree check from the MAJOR finding above.
  - **The test for "Book and README need no edit" is not exact** - A search for `sqlite` in `docs/book/src` gives many correct hits, for example `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md:113-159`. | Suggested fix: Define the test. The book and READMEs must contain no text that names the sqlx features of sessions-postgres, or that says Postgres users get SQLite. The text at `sessions.md:196-199` names only `tls-rustls-aws-lc-rs`, and it stays true.
  - **The facade command is not tested on its own** - The mutation check (line 112-113) makes both commands fail together. | Why it matters: There is no proof that the facade command can fail by itself. | Suggested fix: Add a temporary mutation that only the facade check catches. For example, add `"dep:paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite"` to the facade's `sessions-postgres` feature (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-822/crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml:52`), and confirm that the facade check fails and the crate check passes.
  
  ### QUESTIONS
  - Should the facade check cover more? The facade does not pass `trace-sqlite` through (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml:45`). So the facade with every feature except `sessions-sqlite` must have no SQLite. That one check finds any future crate that pulls in SQLite. Is it in scope?
  - Do you want a CHANGELOG note that names RUSTSEC-2026-0459, as SMA-763 had? This change removes that exposure for Postgres-only users.
  - Did you confirm that release-plz's dependency diff finds a change to features only? The per-crate edits make the release safe either way. The answer decides whether the corrected constraint names both triggers or only the commit trigger.
  - Is a new sqlx user planned, for example a MySQL backend? If so, approach 2 (a minimal base) prevents the same type of leak for `macros` and `migrate`. If not, approach 1 is enough.
  
  ## What's good
  - The diagnosis is exact, including the proc-macro path. In `/Users/smaschek/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-0.9.1/Cargo.toml`, `sqlite` → `sqlite-bundled` → `sqlx-macros?/sqlite` (lines 181-191), and in sqlx-macros-core the `sqlx-sqlite` dependency is optional (`sqlx-macros-core-0.9.1/Cargo.toml:206-212`). So the removal of one feature removes both edges. Postgres keeps `migrate!`: `macros` → `derive` → `sqlx-macros/derive`, which turns on sqlx-macros (sqlx Cargo.toml line 103), and `migrate` → `sqlx-macros?/migrate`. No other workspace crate uses sqlx or gets SQLite from the base: I checked tests/*, the facade examples, the CLI source and sessions-testkit. `core/src/session.rs:1067` names `sqlx::Error` only in a doc comment.

The step goes into a job that is already required, so it needs no ruleset change. `sessions-it` (ci.yml:326) already compiles sessions-postgres outside workspace unification, and its path filter (ci.yml:284-287) runs on this PR. So CI checks once that Postgres compiles without SQLite.
  - Approach 1 is the smallest correct change. It needs no Rust code change, it keeps workspace inheritance, and its analysis of the alternatives (lines 63-74) is correct.

# SMA-822: Move the sqlx `sqlite` feature out of the workspace base

Linear: [SMA-822](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-822). Size: a small change.

## Intent

The root `[workspace.dependencies]` pin of `sqlx` enables the `sqlite` feature.
Every crate that uses `sqlx` inherits it. Thus every user of
`paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres` compiles `libsqlite3-sys` with bundled C
SQLite, and gets every SQLite advisory (for example RUSTSEC-2026-0459, SMA-763),
although the Postgres backend uses no SQLite code.

The baseline on `main` (52a74cca) has two paths from `sessions-postgres` to
`libsqlite3-sys`:

```text
libsqlite3-sys v0.40.0 └── sqlx-sqlite └── sqlx └── paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres
libsqlite3-sys v0.40.0 └── sqlx-sqlite └── sqlx-macros-core └── sqlx-macros (proc-macro) └── sqlx
```

In sqlx 0.9.1, both edges depend on the `sqlite` feature
(`sqlite` → `sqlite-bundled` → `sqlx-macros?/sqlite`, and `sqlx-sqlite` is
optional in `sqlx-macros-core`). Thus the removal of the one feature removes
both edges. `macros` and `migrate` do not need `sqlite`.

## Goals

- Only the crates that use SQLite enable the `sqlx` `sqlite` feature:
  `paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite` and `paigasus-helikon-evals` (through its
  `trace-sqlite` feature).
- `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres -i libsqlite3-sys -e normal,build`
  finds no path.
- A CI step fails if SQLite comes back into the `sessions-postgres` graph, or if
  a SQLite crate loses the feature.
- The published `sessions-postgres` manifest on crates.io loses `sqlite` in the
  next release.

## Non-goals

- No change to the Rust code of any crate.
- No change to the `deny.toml` or `.cargo/audit.toml` advisory lists.
- No change to how `sessions-sqlite` builds SQLite (bundled stays).
- No check of the full facade feature set without `sessions-sqlite`. That list
  needs an enumeration of every facade feature, and the enumeration drifts. The
  targeted checks below cover the known leak.

## Anti-goals

- `sessions-postgres` must not lose `migrate!` or the `macros` feature.
- `sessions-sqlite` and `evals --features trace-sqlite` must not lose any `sqlx`
  feature that they have today.
- `Cargo.lock` must not change. Features are not recorded in the lockfile.

## Constraints

- Workspace inheritance is mandatory (CLAUDE.md). Each crate keeps
  `sqlx = { workspace = true, ... }` and adds its own `features`.
- **Semver: patch.** `sqlx` types are in the public API (`PgPool` in
  `sessions-postgres`, `SqlitePool` in `sessions-sqlite`). The API of
  `sessions-postgres` does not change. A downstream crate that got `sqlx::sqlite`
  only through feature unification with `sessions-postgres` depended on a side
  effect that we never documented. A breaking bump would also force a breaking
  bump of the facade (`scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh`) with no API change.
  There are two failure modes for such a downstream crate, and the upgrade note
  names both:
  - `sqlx::sqlite` items do not compile.
  - `sqlx::AnyPool` with a `sqlite:` URL compiles but fails at run time, because
    `install_default_drivers` registers the SQLite driver only under
    `cfg(feature = "_sqlite")`.
- **Release triggers.** release-plz releases a crate for two independent
  reasons: (a) a commit touches a file in the crate directory, and (b) the
  packaged crate differs from its registry copy. SMA-763 changed only the root
  `sqlx` pin, and `sessions-postgres` 0.1.10 still got a release with the entry
  "update Cargo.toml dependencies". That precedent was a version-requirement
  change. We did not confirm that a feature-only change gives the same diff. So
  each of the three crates also gets a file change in its own directory
  (trigger a): `sessions-sqlite` and `evals` get `features = ["sqlite"]`, and
  `sessions-postgres` gets a CHANGELOG upgrade note and a corrected comment.
  The comment edit exists for this reason. The post-merge check below is the
  real safeguard. The facade and CLI cascade is automatic; no version is
  bumped by hand.
- **Commit scope.** `sessions-postgres` is not an allowed scope (`.versionrc`).
  PR title: `fix(sessions): SMA-822 stop sessions-postgres from compiling sqlite`.
  release-plz writes this line into each CHANGELOG, so it must be true for all
  three crates. It is true: SQLite is enabled where it is used and nowhere else.

## Approaches

1. **Remove only `sqlite` from the base (chosen).** The base keeps
   `runtime-tokio`, `macros`, and `migrate`, which all three crates use. Each
   SQLite crate adds `features = ["sqlite"]`. This is the smallest change and
   matches the ticket.
2. **Make the base minimal (`runtime-tokio` only).** Each crate lists every
   feature it uses. This prevents the same kind of leak for a future
   non-macro user (for example a MySQL backend). No such crate is planned, and
   all three current crates use `macros` and `migrate`. Rejected for now
   (my call).
3. **Add a second workspace entry (`sqlx-sqlite`).** Cargo does not allow two
   `[workspace.dependencies]` keys for one package without a rename. A rename
   changes the name in the code. Rejected.

## Design

1. Root `Cargo.toml`, line 84: remove `"sqlite"` from the `sqlx` feature list.
   Result: `features = ["runtime-tokio", "macros", "migrate"]`. Add a comment
   above the entry: only `sessions-sqlite` and `evals`/`trace-sqlite` enable
   `sqlite` (SMA-822), and a `build-no-default-features` step fails if SQLite
   gets into `sessions-postgres`.
2. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite/Cargo.toml`:
   `sqlx = { workspace = true, features = ["sqlite"] }`.
3. `crates/paigasus-helikon-evals/Cargo.toml`:
   `sqlx = { workspace = true, optional = true, features = ["sqlite"] }`.
   `trace-sqlite = ["dep:sqlx"]` stays.
4. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/Cargo.toml`: update the comment on
   line 18 so that it names the new base (`runtime-tokio`, `macros`, `migrate`,
   and no `sqlite`).
5. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/CHANGELOG.md`, under
   `## [Unreleased]`: a hand-written upgrade note. It says that the crate no
   longer enables the sqlx `sqlite` feature, so Postgres-only users do not
   compile bundled SQLite or get SQLite advisories such as RUSTSEC-2026-0459. It
   says that a crate which uses `sqlx::sqlite`, or `AnyPool` with a `sqlite:`
   URL, must add `features = ["sqlite"]` to its own `sqlx` dependency. The note
   goes on the feature branch, not into the release PR, because release-plz
   drops edits to the release PR when it makes the PR again.
6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `build-no-default-features`: add one step
   `Assert SQLite only where it is used`. It uses
   `cargo tree --color never --target all -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys` with
   these packages:
   - **Negative:** `-p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres`, and
     `-p paigasus-helikon --no-default-features --features sessions-postgres`
     (the facade path most users take). Each must find no path.
   - **Positive controls:** `-p paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite`, and
     `-p paigasus-helikon-evals --features trace-sqlite`. Each must print a tree
     that names `libsqlite3-sys`.

   How to read "no path": with cargo 1.99, when the package is not in the
   graph, `cargo tree -i` exits 101 and writes
   `error: package ID specification ... did not match any packages` to stderr.
   An older form exits 0 and writes `warning: nothing to print` to stderr. The
   negative check passes only if one of those two outcomes occurs and stdout is
   empty. Any other outcome fails the step, and the step prints the output. A
   typo in the package name gives the same error as "no path". The positive
   controls use the same spelling, so they prove on every run that the name
   and the command form still find `libsqlite3-sys`. Each failure writes an
   `::error::` line that says what to fix. The step resolves the graph only, so
   it does not build. The step must not depend on `pipefail`: capture each
   command's stdout, stderr, and exit code separately, then test them.
7. `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`, line 11: add the new step to the list of
   `build-no-default-features` steps (SMA-822).

## Book and README

The test: no page in `docs/book/src` and no `README.md` of the three crates
names the sqlx features of `sessions-postgres`, or says that Postgres users get
SQLite. `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md` names only `tls-rustls-aws-lc-rs`
for Postgres, and that stays true. The builder confirms this with a search and
records the result in the PR body.

## Verification

Before merge:

- The `cargo tree` command from the ticket finds no path.
- `git diff --exit-code "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" -- Cargo.lock`
  passes.
- `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres` (lib only, no dev-deps)
  passes, so `migrate!` works without `sqlite`.
- `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite` and
  `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-evals --features trace-sqlite` pass alone.
- The guard step, run locally as a script, passes on the branch.
- Mutation checks, each reverted after the run:
  - Put `"sqlite"` back into the root base: both negative checks fail.
  - Add `"dep:paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite"` to the facade's
    `sessions-postgres` feature: only the facade check fails.
  - Remove `features = ["sqlite"]` from `evals`: only the `evals` positive
    control fails.
- `cargo package -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres --no-verify`, then read
  `Cargo.toml` from the `.crate` archive by exact name. The `[dependencies.sqlx]`
  features must not include `sqlite`. Do the same for `sessions-sqlite` and
  `evals`; there `sqlite` must be present.
- All CI gates from CLAUDE.md pass locally where possible. `sessions-it` runs
  in CI and compiles `sessions-postgres` outside workspace unification.

After merge:

- The release PR bumps `sessions-postgres`, `sessions-sqlite`, `evals`, the
  facade, and the CLI. Watch the CI of that PR.
- After publish: a scratchpad project that depends only on the new
  `paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres` version must show no `libsqlite3-sys`
  in `cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys -e normal,build`.

## Rollback

A revert in the repository does not change manifests on crates.io. To roll
back: add `"sqlite"` back to the crate's own `sqlx` features, release a new
patch, and let the facade cascade follow.

## Left to the builder

- The exact text of the comments, the CHANGELOG note, and the `::error::`
  messages.
- Whether the guard is an inline `run:` block or a script under `scripts/`.

# SMA-822: Move the sqlx `sqlite` feature out of the workspace base

Linear: [SMA-822](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-822). Size: a small change.

## Intent

The root `[workspace.dependencies]` pin of `sqlx` enables the `sqlite` feature.
Every crate that uses `sqlx` inherits it. Thus every user of
`paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres` compiles `libsqlite3-sys` with bundled C
SQLite, and gets every SQLite advisory (for example RUSTSEC-2026-0459, SMA-763),
although the Postgres backend uses no SQLite code.

The baseline on `main` (52a74cca) has two paths from `sessions-postgres` to
`libsqlite3-sys`:

```text
libsqlite3-sys v0.40.0 └── sqlx-sqlite └── sqlx └── paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres
libsqlite3-sys v0.40.0 └── sqlx-sqlite └── sqlx-macros-core └── sqlx-macros (proc-macro) └── sqlx
```

In sqlx 0.9.1, both edges depend on the `sqlite` feature
(`sqlite` → `sqlite-bundled` → `sqlx-macros?/sqlite`, and `sqlx-sqlite` is
optional in `sqlx-macros-core`). Thus the removal of the one feature removes
both edges. `macros` and `migrate` do not need `sqlite`.

## Goals

- Only the crates that use SQLite enable the `sqlx` `sqlite` feature:
  `paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite` and `paigasus-helikon-evals` (through its
  `trace-sqlite` feature).
- `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres -i libsqlite3-sys -e normal,build`
  finds no path.
- A CI step fails if SQLite comes back into the `sessions-postgres` graph, or if
  a SQLite crate loses the feature.
- The published `sessions-postgres` manifest on crates.io loses `sqlite` in the
  next release.

## Non-goals

- No change to the Rust code of any crate.
- No change to the `deny.toml` or `.cargo/audit.toml` advisory lists.
- No change to how `sessions-sqlite` builds SQLite (bundled stays).
- No check of the full facade feature set without `sessions-sqlite`. That list
  needs an enumeration of every facade feature, and the enumeration drifts. The
  targeted checks below cover the known leak.

## Anti-goals

- `sessions-postgres` must not lose `migrate!` or the `macros` feature.
- `sessions-sqlite` and `evals --features trace-sqlite` must not lose any `sqlx`
  feature that they have today.
- `Cargo.lock` must not change. Features are not recorded in the lockfile.

## Constraints

- Workspace inheritance is mandatory (CLAUDE.md). Each crate keeps
  `sqlx = { workspace = true, ... }` and adds its own `features`.
- **Semver: patch.** `sqlx` types are in the public API (`PgPool` in
  `sessions-postgres`, `SqlitePool` in `sessions-sqlite`). The API of
  `sessions-postgres` does not change. A downstream crate that got `sqlx::sqlite`
  only through feature unification with `sessions-postgres` depended on a side
  effect that we never documented. A breaking bump would also force a breaking
  bump of the facade (`scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh`) with no API change.
  There are two failure modes for such a downstream crate, and the upgrade note
  names both:
  - `sqlx::sqlite` items do not compile.
  - `sqlx::AnyPool` with a `sqlite:` URL compiles but fails at run time, because
    `install_default_drivers` registers the SQLite driver only under
    `cfg(feature = "_sqlite")`.
- **Release triggers.** release-plz releases a crate for two independent
  reasons: (a) a commit touches a file in the crate directory, and (b) the
  packaged crate differs from its registry copy. SMA-763 changed only the root
  `sqlx` pin, and `sessions-postgres` 0.1.10 still got a release with the entry
  "update Cargo.toml dependencies". That precedent was a version-requirement
  change. We did not confirm that a feature-only change gives the same diff. So
  each of the three crates also gets a file change in its own directory
  (trigger a): `sessions-sqlite` and `evals` get `features = ["sqlite"]`, and
  `sessions-postgres` gets a CHANGELOG upgrade note and a corrected comment.

  real safeguard. The facade and CLI cascade is automatic; no version is
  bumped by hand.

  PR title: `fix(sessions): SMA-822 stop sessions-postgres from compiling sqlite`.
  release-plz writes this line into each CHANGELOG, so it must be true for all
  three crates. It is true: SQLite is enabled where it is used and nowhere else.

1. **Remove only `sqlite` from the base (chosen).** The base keeps
   `runtime-tokio`, `macros`, and `migrate`, which all three crates use. Each
   SQLite crate adds `features = ["sqlite"]`. This is the smallest change and
   matches the ticket.
2. **Make the base minimal (`runtime-tokio` only).** Each crate lists every
   feature it uses. This prevents the same kind of leak for a future
   non-macro user (for example a MySQL backend). No such crate is planned, and
   all three current crates use `macros` and `migrate`. Rejected for now
   (my call).
3. **Add a second workspace entry (`sqlx-sqlite`).** Cargo does not allow two
   `[workspace.dependencies]` keys for one package without a rename. A rename
   changes the name in the code. Rejected.

   above the entry: only `sessions-sqlite` and `evals`/`trace-sqlite` enable
   `sqlite` (SMA-822), and a `build-no-default-features` step fails if SQLite
   gets into `sessions-postgres`.
2. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite/Cargo.toml`:
   `sqlx = { workspace = true, features = ["sqlite"] }`.
3. `crates/paigasus-helikon-evals/Cargo.toml`:
   `sqlx = { workspace = true, optional = true, features = ["sqlite"] }`.
   `trace-sqlite = ["dep:sqlx"]` stays.
4. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/Cargo.toml`: update the comment on
   line 18 so that it names the new base (`runtime-tokio`, `macros`, `migrate`,
   and no `sqlite`).
5. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/CHANGELOG.md`, under
   `## [Unreleased]`: a hand-written upgrade note. It says that the crate no
   longer enables the sqlx `sqlite` feature, so Postgres-only users do not
   compile bundled SQLite or get SQLite advisories such as RUSTSEC-2026-0459. It
   says that a crate which uses `sqlx::sqlite`, or `AnyPool` with a `sqlite:`
   URL, must add `features = ["sqlite"]` to its own `sqlx` dependency. The note
   goes on the feature branch, not into the release PR, because release-plz
   drops edits to the release PR when it makes the PR again.
6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `build-no-default-features`: add one step
   `Assert SQLite only where it is used`. It uses
   `cargo tree --color never --target all -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys` with
   these packages:
   - **Negative:** `-p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres`, and
     `-p paigasus-helikon --no-default-features --features sessions-postgres`
     (the facade path most users take). Each must find no path.
   - **Positive controls:** `-p paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite`, and
     `-p paigasus-helikon-evals --features trace-sqlite`. Each must print a tree

   typo in the package name gives the same error as "no path". The positive
   controls use the same spelling, so they prove on every run that the name
   and the command form still find `libsqlite3-sys`. Each failure writes an
   `::error::` line that says what to fix. The step resolves the graph only, so
   it does not build. The step must not depend on `pipefail`: capture each
   command's stdout, stderr, and exit code separately, then test them.
7. `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`, line 11: add the new step to the list of
   `build-no-default-features` steps (SMA-822).

# SMA-822: Move the sqlx `sqlite` feature out of the workspace base

Linear: [SMA-822](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-822). Size: a small change.

## Intent

The root `[workspace.dependencies]` pin of `sqlx` enables the `sqlite` feature.
Every crate that uses `sqlx` inherits it. Thus every user of
`paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres` compiles `libsqlite3-sys` with bundled C
SQLite, and gets every SQLite advisory (for example RUSTSEC-2026-0459, SMA-763),
although the Postgres backend uses no SQLite code.

The baseline on `main` (52a74cca) has two paths from `sessions-postgres` to
`libsqlite3-sys`:

```text
libsqlite3-sys v0.40.0 └── sqlx-sqlite └── sqlx └── paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres
libsqlite3-sys v0.40.0 └── sqlx-sqlite └── sqlx-macros-core └── sqlx-macros (proc-macro) └── sqlx
```

## Goals

- Only the crates that use SQLite enable the `sqlx` `sqlite` feature:
  `paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite` and `paigasus-helikon-evals` (through its
  `trace-sqlite` feature).
- `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres -i libsqlite3-sys -e normal,build`
  finds no path.
- A CI step fails if SQLite comes back into the `sessions-postgres` graph.
- The published `sessions-postgres` manifest on crates.io loses `sqlite` in the
  next release.

## Non-goals

- No change to the Rust code of any crate.
- No change to the `deny.toml` or `.cargo/audit.toml` advisory lists.
- No change to how `sessions-sqlite` builds SQLite (bundled stays).

## Anti-goals

- `sessions-postgres` must not lose `migrate!` or the `macros` feature.
- `sessions-sqlite` and `evals --features trace-sqlite` must not lose any `sqlx`
  feature that they have today.

## Constraints

- Workspace inheritance is mandatory (CLAUDE.md). Each crate keeps
  `sqlx = { workspace = true, ... }` and adds its own `features`.
- `sqlx` types are in the public API: `PgPool` in `sessions-postgres`,
  `SqlitePool` in `sessions-sqlite`. A downstream crate that used
  `sqlx::sqlite` only because `sessions-postgres` turned it on stops compiling.
  We never documented that feature as part of the `sessions-postgres` API, so
  this change is a patch release, not a breaking release. The CHANGELOG entry
  from the `fix` commit says that the feature is gone.
- release-plz bumps a crate from the commits that touch files in that crate's
  directory. A change to the root `Cargo.toml` only does not get a release for
  `sessions-postgres`, so crates.io keeps the old manifest. Each of the three
  crates must have a file change in its own directory. Each `Cargo.toml` changes
  anyway (`sessions-sqlite` and `evals` get `features = ["sqlite"]`,
  `sessions-postgres` gets the corrected comment). The PR title uses the `fix`
  type, so the squashed commit gives a patch bump. The facade cascade is
  automatic; no version is bumped by hand.

## Approaches

1. **Remove only `sqlite` from the base (chosen).** The base keeps
   `runtime-tokio`, `macros`, and `migrate`, which all three crates use. Each
   SQLite crate adds `features = ["sqlite"]`. This is the smallest change and
   matches the ticket.
2. **Make the base minimal (`runtime-tokio` only).** Each crate lists every
   feature it uses. This is more explicit, but it changes three crates' feature
   lists for no user gain. All three crates use `macros` and `migrate` today.
3. **Add a second workspace entry (`sqlx-sqlite`).** Cargo does not allow two
   `[workspace.dependencies]` keys for one package without a rename. A rename
   changes the name in the code. Rejected.

## Design

1. Root `Cargo.toml`, line 84: remove `"sqlite"` from the `sqlx` feature list.
   Result: `features = ["runtime-tokio", "macros", "migrate"]`.
2. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite/Cargo.toml`:
   `sqlx = { workspace = true, features = ["sqlite"] }`.
3. `crates/paigasus-helikon-evals/Cargo.toml`:
   `sqlx = { workspace = true, optional = true, features = ["sqlite"] }`.
   `trace-sqlite = ["dep:sqlx"]` stays.
4. `crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/Cargo.toml`: update the comment on
   line 18 so that it names the new base (`runtime-tokio`, `macros`, `migrate`,
   and no `sqlite`).
5. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `build-no-default-features`: add a step
   `Assert no SQLite under sessions-postgres`. It runs
   `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys`
   and fails if the output names `libsqlite3-sys`. It must test the output, not
   the exit code. The builder must confirm what `cargo tree -i` prints and
   returns when the package is not in the graph, before and after the change.
   The step uses the same shape as the existing axum and `vendored-protox`
   steps: an `::error::` line that says what to fix. It resolves the graph only,
   so it does not build.
6. The step also checks the facade with only `sessions-postgres` on:
   `cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon --no-default-features --features sessions-postgres -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys`.
   This is the path most users take.
7. Update `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` with one line about the new step
   in the `build-no-default-features` section, if that section lists its steps.

## Book and README

The mdBook and the crate READMEs do not name the `sqlx` features, so they need
no change. The builder confirms this with a search for `sqlite` in
`docs/book/src` and in the three crates' `README.md`.

## Verification

- The `cargo tree` command from the ticket finds no path.
- The guard fails on `main` (mutation check: put `"sqlite"` back into the base
  and run the step locally) and passes on the branch.
- `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres` (lib only, no dev-deps)
  passes, so `migrate!` works without `sqlite`.
- `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite` and
  `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-evals --features trace-sqlite` pass alone.
- `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-evals --no-default-features` passes.
- All CI gates from CLAUDE.md pass locally where possible. `sessions-it` runs
  in CI.

## Left to the builder

- The exact text of the `Cargo.toml` comment and the `::error::` message.
- Whether the runbook needs the line (item 7).

## Gate 1: approve the spec

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sqlx-sqlite-feature-out-of-workspace-base-design.md` in the worktree `.worktrees/sma-822`. I have not committed it yet.

**Challenger verdict:** approve with changes. It found no blocker. It confirmed the main design: if you remove `sqlite` from the base, both SQLite paths go away, and `migrate!` still works for Postgres.

**What I changed in the spec:**

1. **My release-plz model was wrong.** SMA-763 changed only the root pin, and `sessions-postgres` 0.1.10 still got a release. I checked this in its CHANGELOG. The spec now names both release triggers. The edits in each crate stay as a second safeguard, and a check after the merge is the real safeguard.
2. **The guard logic is new.** I tested `cargo tree -i` on cargo 1.99. When the package is absent, it exits with code 101 and the message "did not match any packages". A typo in the package name gives the same result. The challenger's version of the guard would therefore fail on a correct branch. The step now accepts only that error or "nothing to print", with empty stdout.
3. **I added positive controls.** `sessions-sqlite` and `evals --features trace-sqlite` must show `libsqlite3-sys`. Workspace feature unification hides a missing `sqlite` feature in every other CI job. Without this check, the problem shows only at publish time, and the publish stops partway.
4. **I added an upgrade note** under `[Unreleased]` in the `sessions-postgres` CHANGELOG. It covers two failures: code that uses `sqlx::sqlite` does not compile, and `AnyPool` with a `sqlite:` URL fails at run time.
5. **I added more verification:** a check of the packaged manifest, three mutation checks, a check that `Cargo.lock` does not change, and checks after the merge and after the publish.
6. **Smaller changes:** the PR scope is `fix(sessions)`, `--target all --color never` are on every command, the runbook edit is now required, the root `Cargo.toml` gets a comment, and the spec has a rollback section.

**Findings I did not take:**

- **A facade check with every feature except `sessions-sqlite`.** That list must name each facade feature, and it would go out of date. I wrote this down as a non-goal.
- **Approach 2 (a base with only `runtime-tokio`).** This helps only if a new `sqlx` user comes, for example a MySQL backend. I do not know of a plan for one. That was my call. Tell me if you plan one.

Do you approve the spec? You can also ask for changes, or run the challenge again with `/challenge-spec`.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Only `sessions-sqlite` and `evals`/`trace-sqlite` enable the sqlx `sqlite` feature, and a CI step keeps it that way.

**Architecture:** A guard script resolves four dependency graphs with `cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys` (two must have no SQLite, two must have it). CI runs it in `build-no-default-features`. Then the manifests change so the guard passes.

**Tech Stack:** Cargo manifests, bash, GitHub Actions.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sqlx-sqlite-feature-out-of-workspace-base-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Every `cargo tree` call uses `--color never --target all -e normal,build -i libsqlite3-sys`.
- Workspace inheritance stays: `sqlx = { workspace = true, ... }` in each crate.
- `Cargo.lock` must not change: `git diff --exit-code "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" -- Cargo.lock`.
- No Rust code changes. No version bumps by hand.
- Commit scopes must be in `.versionrc` (`sessions`, `ci`, `deps`, `workspace`, `plan`, `spec`). No `sessions-postgres` scope.

- Work synchronously in the foreground. Do not background long cargo runs.

## Review Focus

1. A typo in the package name or a cargo output change makes the negative check pass without a check → the positive controls must fail in that case (Task 1, step 2 shows the controls run; Task 2 mutation 3 proves a control can fail).
2. cargo exits 101 with "did not match any packages" for an absent package (cargo 1.99) → the negative check treats that as a pass, not as an error (Task 1, step 2).
3. Workspace feature unification hides a lost `sqlite` feature → per-package `cargo build -p` and the positive controls catch it (Task 2).

- `assert_absent <label> <cargo tree package args...>` passes only if stdout is empty AND either (exit ≠ 0 and stderr contains `did not match any packages`) or (exit = 0 and stderr contains `nothing to print`).
- `assert_present <label> <cargo tree package args...>` passes only if exit = 0 and stdout contains `libsqlite3-sys v`.
